# Skysay Gateway

> Skysay Gateway — the self-hostable LiveKit media plane behind Skysay: livekit-server + livekit-sip + the exported media-plane agent worker + a session reconciler + redis. Call audio (SIP/RTP) terminates on the operator's servers; the Skysay Cloud control plane resolves per-call config, runs tools, and settles billing over HTTPS (see what leaves the operator's servers below). Numbers, KYB/compliance, billing, and abuse policy stay in the control plane.

## Repository map

- [Self-host install runbook](INSTALL.md): the linear, step-by-step self-host guide (prerequisites -> configure -> up -> provision -> smoke test -> test call); every env var documented with what/where-to-get-it/example. START HERE to install.
- [Agent operating instructions](AGENTS.md): how an AI agent should execute the install and work in this repo.
- [Self-host smoke test](packages/skysay-gateway/deploy/selfhost-smoketest.sh): PASS/FAIL verification of the running stack (services, agent registration, the gateway token on both control-plane surfaces it uses); exit 0 proves the safe prerequisites, while the first real call confirms the DID route.
- [LiveKit agent](livekit_agent/): the media-plane agent (minimal pinned Dockerfile); per-call config resolves from the control plane.
- [Self-host quickstart + deploy files](packages/skysay-gateway/deploy/SELFHOST.md): runbook, [docker-compose.livekit.yml](packages/skysay-gateway/deploy/docker-compose.livekit.yml), config templates.
- [skysay-gateway package](packages/skysay-gateway/): caller-side evidence referee and portable RTP codecs; no call runtime or provider registry.
- [skysay-common package](packages/skysay-common/): control-plane-free shared config + runtime helpers.
- [Gateway↔Cloud contract](contracts/gateway-v1.yaml): OpenAPI v1.0.0, stable.
- [JSON Schemas](contracts/schemas/): request/response bodies for the stable surface.
- [README](README.md): overview and quickstart pointers.

## Provenance

Generated from the Skysay source, with documented omissions, substitutions and export transformations.

## What leaves the operator's servers

The gateway runs on your servers and carries the call's audio. From there, audio and text go to your carrier and to the speech and model providers your agent uses. Skysay Cloud receives the call's metadata; during the call, the arguments of each tool call, any knowledge-base question the agent sends and, when the agent has tools that write to your systems, what the caller says; after the call, the recording and transcript.

## The LiveKit media plane

The self-host stack is not identical to Skysay production: livekit-server v1.13.6 + livekit-sip v1.13.0 are the versions this repository intends the production voice box to run (that promotion happens on its own schedule; re-verify against the running containers before relying on it as a live parity claim), while redis 8.8.0 does not track production at all (production is on 7.4.5-alpine); all three are digest-pinned + the `agents` container running [livekit_agent/agent/production_agent.py](livekit_agent/agent/production_agent.py) (LiveKit Agents 1.8.8) + a session `reconciler`. The agent joins each inbound room unsubscribed and admits NO caller audio until the control plane authorizes the call: `POST /v1/calls/inbound/route` (the deployment-bound `skygw_` gateway token) resolves the DID to the authoritative agent, then `GET /v1/calls/{call_id}/realtime-config` (the same token) returns the validated semantic config (system prompt, first message, language, the speech and model stack the agent uses, voice, tool allowlist). Tool schemas come from MCP `tools/list` on `POST /mcp`, are exposed to the model ONLY if allowlisted, and every invocation re-crosses the call-bound `POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/agent-tool-calls` endpoint with an audit trail. Lifecycle events post to `POST /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}/call-lifecycle-events` and produce the authoritative billing verdict; artifacts upload to `POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/artifacts`. The reconciler closes sessions whose agent died so dangling billed minutes are impossible.

## The contract (gateway ↔ Cloud)

The exact surface is [contracts/gateway-v1.yaml](contracts/gateway-v1.yaml) (v1.0.0 stable) plus [contracts/schemas/](contracts/schemas/). Endpoints the stack uses:

- `POST /v1/calls/inbound/route` — resolve an inbound DID to the authoritative agent (gateway token).
- `GET /v1/calls/{call_id}/realtime-config` — the validated per-call semantic config (gateway token).
- `POST /mcp` — MCP `tools/list` schema discovery (gateway token; `tools/list` is the only method it may call).
- `POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/agent-tool-calls` — allowlisted model-tool execution bound to that call.
- `POST /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}/call-lifecycle-events` — lifecycle + authoritative billing verdict (gateway token).
- `POST /v1/calls/{id}/artifacts` — upload call artifacts with duration provenance (gateway token).
- `POST /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}/tokens` / `.../tokens/rotate` — mint / rotate the per-gateway `skygw_` token (shown once).
- `GET /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}/number-rules` — routing read (also the smoke test's gateway-token probe).
- `POST /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}/outbound-calls` — admit an outbound call THIS deployment will dial (gateway token, `local` mode only). Returns the admitted call plus a single-use `tca_` bound to that call; nothing is enqueued.
- `GET /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}` — read `outbound_execution_mode`: this is how an agent tells which originate path it is on.

## Placing an outbound call (which path am I on?)

A deployment is in one of two outbound modes, readable at
`GET /v1/gateway-deployments/{id}` as `outbound_execution_mode`:

- `local` — this box dials its own calls. Ask it to dial:
  `docker compose -f packages/skysay-gateway/deploy/docker-compose.livekit.yml run --rm outbound-worker python /app/outbound_worker.py originate --to +<E164> --purpose <purpose> --reason "<why>"`.
  The control plane runs the full policy + wallet admission and mints the
  call-bound token; no organization-scoped key exists on this box, and a remote
  `POST /v1/calls` for this workspace's numbers is refused with a message that
  names this command.
- `queue` (the default, and every deployment created before local origination)
  — outbound calls are requested from the control plane with an
  organization-scoped API key (`POST /v1/calls`) and this box's
  `--profile outbound` worker claims and dials them.

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer` from `SKYSAY_GATEWAY_API_TOKEN` (`skygw_...`, narrowly scoped to its registered gateway) — the long-lived credential you configure, inbound AND outbound, once the deployment is in `local` outbound mode; during a call the gateway also holds a call authorization and any provider keys leased to it. Its organization is derived server-side from the token row, never from the request body, and `tools/list` is the only MCP method it may call. `SKYSAY_WORKER_API_TOKEN` (`sky_...`, organization-scoped) is needed ONLY by the legacy `queue` outbound mode, where claiming other requesters' call jobs is organization-wide worker-job authority a gateway token deliberately excludes; leave it unset on a `local`-mode box. The transport layer requires https (or verified loopback http) and refuses cross-origin redirects.

## Audio contract

`pcm_s16le_8000_mono` — 16-bit little-endian PCM, 8 kHz, mono. No negotiation.

## Safety boundaries

- The agent admits no caller audio before the control plane authorizes the call and its config validates.
- Tools are model-visible ONLY if allowlisted in realtime-config; every call is auditable at the control plane.
- Bearer tokens never travel plaintext to non-loopback hosts; cross-origin redirects are refused.
- The gateway token is deployment-scoped, so a compromise stops at this deployment's workspace. In `local` outbound mode it is the long-lived credential you configure, and during a call the gateway also holds a call authorization and any provider keys leased to it; the legacy `queue` mode's `sky_` key is organization-scoped and widens that blast radius knowingly. Protect the host, rotate on suspicion ([SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)).
- Outbound origination never bypasses the control plane: this box cannot reach media without a single-use `tca_` the control plane mints only after its own policy decision, caps, kill switches and wallet reserve have passed.
